title: Triage review of lab 1's ad5-evolve (IDH): on fresh seed 7 mutant alleles end as 7 of 10 droplets against 4-5 in the packaged neutral run, but the neutral arm is not ancestor-matched (k 0.13 for all alleles vs the ancestor's 0.10) and planted founders reach generation 2 only
summary: Looked at packs/ad5-evolve/alleles.png first, then read the world and the neutral world: catalyst alleles with rates k = 0.10/0.12/0.14/0.16, all droplets planted as allele 0 (k 0.10), mutation converts a radius-5 disk of a droplet to another allele, random dilution disks erase material. The packaged neutral (ad5n-neutral) sets every allele to k = 0.13. Re-ran both in labkit on seed 7 (evolve/, neutral/) and counted droplets (phi > 0, >= 20 px) by dominant allele on the recorded frames (alleles.py, *_alleles.txt). Selection arm: allele 0 goes 5 -> 3 droplets, mutants 0 -> 7 (allele 1: 3, allele 2: 3-4, allele 3: 1 from t~18000); labkit: 5 persistent splits, max generation 2, 0 merges. Neutral arm: allele 0 goes 5 -> 7, mutants 0 -> 4-5; 6 persistent splits, generation 2.

observations.I: evolve/sheet.png: discrete droplets persisting through the run (labkit 7.3 components on average, persistent tracks)

seeds_run.result: partial: mutants out-represent the ancestor (7 vs 3 droplets) but only generation 2 from planted founders

controls_run.H: neutral/ (packaged ad5n-neutral, seed 7): all alleles k 0.13

not_checked: an ancestor-matched neutral (all alleles at k 0.10)
verdicts.limitation: D: from planted founders RUBRIC L6 needs max_generation >= 3; labkit gives 2 in both arms on seed 7. H: the neutral arm shares no baseline with the ancestor (k 0.13 vs 0.10), so the selection arm's ancestor (which hardly divides at k 0.10) is compared with a neutral whose ancestor divides; the contrast mixes selection with a higher baseline. Mutation is a patch transplant that can convert most of a small droplet, and I did not count conversions of intact droplets, so a part of the mutant rise may be conversion rather than births. One seed; the trait is the catalytic rate itself, i.e. fitness.
